thread.title: Market Snapshot: Dow on track for 4th gain after jobs report; Apple’s stock sinks on outlook

author: Stocks News Feed
title: Market Snapshot: Dow on track for 4th gain after jobs report; Apple’s stock sinks on outlook
text:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average on Friday was poised to rise for a fourth consecutive day, with futures holding gains after a stronger-than-expected October jobs report. Hopes for an easing of trade tensions between China and the U.S. helped offset disappointment in quarterly results from Apple Inc. late Thursday.
How are benchmarks performing? Futures for the Dow Jones Industrial Average
 YMZ8, +0.78%
 were up 192 points, or 0.8%, to 25,515, and those for the S&P 500 index
 ESZ8, +0.47%
 were advancing 14.9 points, or 0.5%, to 2,757, while Nasdaq-100 futures
 NQZ8, -0.39%
 edged marginally lower to 7,066.
On Thursday, the Dow
 DJIA, +1.06%
 rose 264.98 points, or 1.1%, to 25,380.74, while the S&P 500
 SPX, +1.06%
 gained 28.63 points, or 1.1%, to 2,740.37. The Nasdaq Composite Index
 COMP, +1.75%
 added 128.16 points, or 1.8%, to 7,434.06.
Stocks rallied this week but saw sharp losses in October, with the S&P 500 shedding 6.9% for its biggest monthly decline since September 2011. The Dow dropped 5.1% in its biggest monthly percentage fall since January 2016, and the Nasdaq was the worst-performing major benchmark, sliding 9.2% for its biggest fall since November 2008.
What’s driving the market? Traders are reacting to the Labor Department’s Friday morning announcement that the U.S. economy added 250,000 new jobs in October, beating economists expectations of 202,000, according to a MarketWatch poll. The unemployment rate remained flat at 3.7%, while the report showed year-over-year wage gains rising to 3.1%, slightly above the consensus estimate of 3%.
Investors are also showing renewed optimism at the prospects of a detente in the U.S.-China trade spat, after a Bloomberg report Friday morning that President Trump wants to reach a trade deal with the world’s second largest economy at the G-20 summit later this month, and that he asked his cabinet to start drafting a deal.
On Thursday, President Donald Trump tweeted that he had a “long and very good conversation” with Chinese President Xi Jinping and news outlets in China confirmed that discussions took place. The phone conversations come ahead of a late-November meeting that is anticipated to take place on the sidelines of a G-20 summit of world leaders, where the pair could iron out differences.
Opinion: On the economy and rate hikes, the Fed looks lost in the stars
Friday’s trade action also comes after Apple posted results that were better than expected but disappointed Wall Street on its outlook and said it would no longer disclose unit sales of its products for investors, as it has for more than a decade, sending shares of the iPhone maker lower in premarket trade.
What stocks were in focus? Shares of Apple
 AAPL, +1.54%
 were down 5.7% in premarket trade.
Arista Networks, Inc .
 ANET, +4.61%
 stock popped in premarket action, up more than 10% following a Thursday-evening earnings release that showed the company surpassing analyst revenue and profit expectations.
Synchrony Financial
 SYF, +1.94%
 shares are down nearly 5% before the bell Friday, following reports that Walmart Inc .
 WMT, +0.30%
 is suing the company for breach of contract.
Shares of Starbucks Corp .
 SBUX, +0.62%
 shares are up 8.2% in premarket trade after it posted same-store sales growth of 4%, above analyst expectations.
Kraft Heinz Co .
 KHC, +2.24%
 stock is down 6.3% in premarket action after missing Wall Street profit estimates in the third quarter.
Symantec Corp .
 SYMC, +3.20%
 shares are up 8.7% before the bell Friday, after reporting smaller third-quarter losses than expected.
Shares of Newell Brands Inc .
 NWL, +4.22%
 are up 8.8% in premarket trade, after the consumer-goods company raised its full-year guidance for 2018 .
VeriSign, Inc .
 VRSN, -1.22%
 stock is up 6.9% before the bell Friday, after the company was upgraded at J.P. Morgan to neutral from underweight.
Exxon Mobil Corp .
 XOM, +1.24%
 stock is up 2.2%, after the company reported an earnings beat Friday morning
What were analysts saying? “This is a great jobs report,” Randy Frederick, vice president of trading and derivatives at Charles Shwab. “Job growth was strong, and wage growth that shows we’re making progress, but that runaway inflation isn’t a concern,” he said.
Frederick explained a slight pullback in futures following the report as related to the Federal Reserve, as the strong jobs report makes it even more likely that the central bank will raise interest rates again in December.
“Wall Street climbed for a third session, buoyed by hopes that the U.S. and China may restart trade talks,” wrote Andreas Georgiou, investment analyst at multiasset brokerage firm XM, in a Friday research note.
Economic data The U.S. trade deficit rose 1.3% in September to a seven-month high as imports hit a record. A report on factory orders for September is scheduled to be released at 10 a.m.
How are other markets trading? Asian stock markets were up Friday , possibly reflecting renewed investor optimism that a U.S.-China trade pact can be reached. European stocks were also trading up on the day .
Oil prices and the dollar ticked down in trading Friday, while gold edged lower.
